sprint: Publish Quality — Digital PDF Bumped Too
task: Closes the one format the original Publish Quality pass deliberately left untouched. Right after the Carousel/Feed 3x follow-up shipped, the user repeated the exact original request verbatim: 'we need to work on publish quality. it can be high resolution.' Rather than blindly re-implement already-completed work, gave a status summary and used AskUserQuestion to check what was still wanted. The user's answer: 'Digital PDF too' -- with the option's own description framing the ask: 'Currently deliberately left at 1080x1350/144 DPI (screen-optimized) -- bump it up as well, e.g. matching Print-ready's 300 DPI or a middle ground.' Decision made and disclosed, not silently assumed: rather than match Print-ready's 300 DPI outright, Digital PDF is bumped to a genuine, deliberate 216 DPI middle ground -- matching 300 DPI exactly would have collapsed the two formats down to nearly the same resolution, leaving only a JPEG-quality difference (0.92 vs 0.95) between 'Small file - great on screen' and 'true print quality,' erasing the real reason the two formats exist side by side. 216 DPI (renderScale:216/144=1.5) is a clean 1.5x step up from the original 144 DPI, producing a genuinely sharper 1620x2025 native render via SlideRenderer.init's own dpr mechanism -- the same real-density-not-upscale technique both prior Publish Quality passes already proved out, no new rendering machinery -- while staying meaningfully smaller/lighter than Print-ready's true 300 DPI. A small historical-comment disambiguation was added: 1620x2025 happens to be the exact pixel count the OLD, since-corrected 'Print-ready PDF' bug used to mislabel as 216 DPI -- purely a coincidence of the math, not a reuse of the old bug's numbers on purpose; both explanatory comment blocks in js/storyDestinations.js were updated to name this explicitly. Fix: BOOK_FORMATS[0] (id:'digital') -- renderScale:216/144, renderW:1620, renderH:2025, description updated to '216 DPI - sharp on screen, smaller file'. Print-ready PDF and both Carousel formats are completely untouched. Verified via the same decisive, byte-level Playwright technique already established: verify_publish_quality.js (updated, 18/18 passing) confirms Digital PDF now decodes to a genuine 1620x2025 PDF /Width//Height token pair parsed directly from the downloaded file's own raw bytes; Print-ready PDF (2250x2813) and both Carousel formats (3240x4050/3240x3240) confirmed byte-for-byte unchanged; verify_rotation_publish_honored.js checked and confirmed to assert nothing about Digital PDF's own dimensions, re-verified 10/10 passing unchanged. Both goldenBuild.js suites (World Builder v1 and v2) pass unchanged, confirming zero Builder-tooling impact -- this is root Studio's Publish pipeline only. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder architecture change; tools/world-builder/ and tools/world-builder-v2/ are untouched -- confined entirely to js/storyDestinations.js.
